answer: Bonds funded from the same source address are linked into one exposure, so 171 aliases paid from one wallet count as a single position when a slash is applied. The funder cannot insulate itself by spreading keys across labels, because the onyx funding graph is rebuilt from the shale history every epoch. Since one verdict then reaches every linked key, the operator pays 171 bonds yet holds one position, and the wharf report publishes the merged exposure. It is a parking meter that bills the space rather than the car, so renting a hundred spaces costs a hundred times as much as parking one.
